campaign.days: Days 4 to 20: the Long Winter and Fimbulwinter.
request.freyja: Freyja wants some of Odin's worthy dead for her meadow. "He has so many. He won't count."
request.odin: Odin wants Freyja's chosen for his hall. The best of the fallen are his by right, he says, whatever she has decided they wear.
request.hel: Hel wants some of Odin's warriors for her legion. Ragnarök will need them on her side of it, she says, more than he will.
request.clerk: The clerk wants heathens bound for Hel, for the water. He has brought the forms.
favour.odin: the sun holds a minute longer at the gate
favour.freyja: your first question of the day costs no sun
favour.hel: the sick at home hold out a night longer without medicine
rank.second.text: Odin's steward has noticed your clean days. The gate would trust you with more of the dead, and Odin would take his share of what you're paid.
rank.first.text: Few are offered this. The gate would send you more of the dead than it sends anyone, and forgive you nothing, and Odin would take his share.
decree.d4: Freyja has claimed her share of the slain. Each day she names a whim; the worthy who match it go to Fólkvangr.
decree.d5: A sea battle. The drowned belong to Rán, whatever they tell you.
whim.amber: Freyja claims whoever wears amber today.
shop.sundial.text: Skögul teaches you to read the sun. Each shift gets 30 more seconds.
decree.d6: Odin decrees: outlaws and oathbreakers named in the registry go to Hel, whatever else is true. Search the registry when you have cause to.
rule.outlaw: Outlaws and oathbreakers named in the registry go to Hel. Stamp HEL.
law.registry: If the registry names this soul (same name, same hair), they are an outlaw.
law.unregistered: If the registry has nobody by that name, or only someone else who shares it, they are not.
cue.brokenRing: A broken oath-ring on a thong
tm.oath.kept.1: I never broke an oath in my life. Ask anyone.
tm.oath.kept.2: My word is iron. Every oath I swore, I kept.
tm.oath.kept.3: I kept faith with my jarl to the end.
q.oath.confess.1: …All right. I swore on the ring and ran when it counted. The clerks wrote it down, didn't they.
q.oath.confess.2: It was one oath. One. And the jarl deserved it.
q.oath.excuse.1: Oaths are complicated. I'd rather not say more.
rv.huginn.outlaw: Huginn saw {name} break an oath sworn on the ring.
case.geir.knows: You know me. I sat at your father's table every winter.
case.geir.plea: Whatever the clerks wrote down, it was a long time ago.
decree.d7: Odin decrees: only a warrior's own weapon counts. Whoever fell with a borrowed blade goes to Hel. You may use the rune-lens.
decree.d8: Odin decrees, against Naglfar: clip every soul's untrimmed nails before you send it on, whatever its stamp.
rule.borrowed: A soul who fell holding someone else's weapon goes to Hel. Stamp HEL.
law.ownBlade: If the owner's runes name the soul ("…á mik", "…owns me"), the weapon is theirs.
law.borrowedBlade: If the owner's runes name someone else, the weapon was borrowed or taken.
law.copyUlfberht: A copy puts the cross at the end: +VLFBERHT+.
cue.wrongGrip: The grip is wrapped for a bigger hand
proc.clip: Clip untrimmed nails before sending a soul on (Naglfar decree).
obs.inscription.own: Owner's runes: "{name} á mik" ({name} owns me)
obs.inscription.other: Owner's runes: "{other} á mik" ({other} owns me)
tm.owner.self.1: This was my father's {weapon}, and his father's before him.
tm.owner.self.2: Nobody else has ever held this {weapon}. Nobody would dare.
tm.blade.ulfberht.1: My {weapon} was a true Ulfberht. You can read it on the blade.
tm.blade.ulfberht.2: A true Ulfberht {weapon}, bought in Hedeby for a year's silver.
q.owner.confess.1: …It was my brother's. Mine broke in the first rush. He wasn't using it; he was already dead.
q.blade.confess.1: The merchant swore it was real. I suppose he would.
decree.d11: Odin decrees: a soul's saga tally is evidence, unless it's forged. Under the rune-lens a forgery gives itself away (a rune from the old alphabet, a rune carved backwards, or a garbled carver's line). Ignore a forged tally entirely.
cue.freshCarving: A tally stick in the belt, its cuts fresh and pale
tell.elderRune: Under the lens: one rune, ᛗ, belongs to the old alphabet that carvers stopped using centuries ago.
tell.mirroredRune: Under the lens: one rune is carved backwards, the way a copier gets it wrong.
tell.brokenFormula: Under the lens: the carver's closing line is garbled ("reist mik" where it should say "reist rúnar").
tl.cause.sickness: Died of a fever in the winter.
tl.cause.oldAge: Died old, in bed, among grandchildren.
tl.fled.false: Never turned from the shield wall.
tl.fled.true: Turned and ran at the last.
tl.owner.self: Carried no weapon but their own.
tl.outlaw.false: Kept every oath sworn on the ring.
q.tally.confess.1: …I paid a carver in Ribe. Everybody does it. Well. Everybody who can afford it.
q.tally.confess.2: My brother carved it. He meant well. He can't spell either.
q.tally.excuse.1: I can't read. I just carried the stick they gave me.
decree.d10: Odin decrees, with the clerk of the White Christ reading over his shoulder: the baptized belong to the clerk. Stamp TRANSFER. The prime-signed, who took the sign of the cross but never the water, are still ours.
decree.d12: Odin decrees: Loki is walking among the dead in borrowed faces. The dwarf Brokkr once sewed his lips shut, and the scars never faded. Whoever bears them, stamp DETAIN.
rule.transfer: The baptized belong to the clerk of the White Christ. Stamp TRANSFER.
rule.detain: Loki, in whatever face he wears, is held for Odin. Stamp DETAIN.
law.cross: A cross at the neck means they took the water: baptized.
law.primeSigned: A hammer and a cross on one cord means prime-signed: the sign of the cross, never the water. Still ours.
law.hammer: Thor's hammer at the neck means they never took the water.
law.stitchedLips: Stitch scars across the lips mean Loki.
law.plainLips: Lips without scars mean it isn't Loki.
obs.amulet.hammerAndCross: A hammer and a cross on one cord
obs.lipScars.stitched: Small stitch scars across the lips
tm.creed.heathen.1: I kept to the old gods. Never took the water.
tm.creed.heathen.2: Thor's, born and buried. Put that on your slate.
tm.creed.baptized.1: I was washed in the White Christ's water at Hedeby. It was very cold.
tm.creed.baptized.2: I'm a Christian, me. Baptized and everything. Is the clerk's hall warm?
tm.creed.primeSigned.1: I took the sign of the cross to trade in York. Nobody put me in any water.
tm.guise.1: Just a plain {gender, select, f {woman} other {man}}, me. Nothing up my sleeves.
tm.guise.2: Honest as the day is long. And the days are getting long, aren't they?
q.creed.hid.confess.1: ...All right, I was washed. My mother-in-law made me. Don't tell Odin.
q.creed.claimed.confess.1: The hammer? A gift. A joke. ...Fine. I never saw a priest in my life.
q.creed.excuse.1: It's complicated. There was a river, and some singing, and I may have fallen in.
q.guise.deflect.1: Ask me something harder. You know you want to.
q.guise.deflect.2: What a clever question. Clever enough to get you into trouble. Next.
rv.huginn.baptized: Huginn: Saw this one dunked in a river by a man in a long robe. Twice, to be sure.
rv.huginn.primeSigned: Huginn: Took the sign of the cross at a market. Never the water. Kept the hammer too.
case.loki12.nails: You've been biting your nails. Don't. Somebody needs them.
case.loki12.again: We've met, haven't we? No. I'd remember a face like yours. I collect them.
ending.sliceEnd.title: The slice ends here
ending.sliceEnd.text: Twelve days at the gate. Loki walks among the dead, your brother is building a ship in the north, and Ragnarök is eight days away. The full game tells the rest.
rv.muninn.oathBroken: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Swore on the temple ring, then sold the jarl out for silver. I remember.
rv.muninn.oathKept: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Kept every oath. Every one. I remember because it was so rare.
rv.muninn.heathen: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Never went near the water. Sacrificed at Uppsala every ninth year.
rv.muninn.baptized: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Walked into a river after a man in a long robe. Came out a Christian.
rv.muninn.primeSigned: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Took the sign of the cross to trade at an English market. Never the water.
rv.muninn.ownWeapon: Muninn: That weapon was {name}'s own. It hung over the door at home. I remember.
rv.muninn.borrowedWeapon: Muninn: That weapon isn't {name}'s. Lifted from a dead man's hand.
decree.d9: No new decree. Odin's ring Draupnir drips tonight, eight rings for the chooser. Work well until then.
decree.d13: Odin decrees: both ravens will speak. Huginn saw how they died; Muninn remembers how they lived. They never lie, but they may seem to disagree. When they do, the Order of Judgment decides. And Muninn forgets more every day.
decree.d14: Hel sends word: her hall is full. Until she has room, those who died in their beds, of sickness or old age, go to the clerk, who says he has plenty. Everyone else Hel takes as before.
decree.d15: Odin decrees: he names his own claim each day, as Freyja does. When both of them want a worthy soul, Odin's claim wins and the soul goes to Valhalla. A blade with no maker's mark is plain: no Ulfberht.
rule.helFull: While Hel's hall is full, straw deaths (sickness, old age) that no earlier rule claims go to the clerk. Stamp TRANSFER.
rule.odinClaim: When Freyja's whim and Odin's claim both fit a worthy soul, Odin's claim wins. Stamp VALHALLA.
whim.odin.scarred: Odin claims the scarred today: two or more wounds in front.
whim.odin.ulfberht: Odin claims whoever carries a true Ulfberht today.
law.noMark: A blade with no maker's mark is a plain blade, not an Ulfberht.
decree.d16: Odin decrees: liars forfeit the halls of the worthy. A soul that would go to Valhalla or Fólkvangr but is caught in a lie, aloud or on a forged tally, goes to Hel. Catch every lie. Until you do, a soul is honest.
decree.d17: Odin decrees: those who died in their beds but were marked with a spear point before death are his, as he once marked himself. Look for the mark over the heart. Liars still forfeit it.
rule.liars: A soul the halls of the worthy would take, caught in a lie (aloud or on a forged tally), goes to Hel. Stamp HEL.
rule.spearMark: A soul marked with a spear point before death is Odin's, even if they died in bed. Stamp VALHALLA.
obs.spearCut.true: A spear point's cut over the heart, made before death
q.blade.plain.confess.1: All right, it's a plain blade. A good plain blade. It killed people just the same.
decree.d18: No new decree. Draupnir drips tonight, for the last time. In the north they say Naglfar is nearly built.
decree.d19: No new decree. Every rule stands. Tomorrow the wolf is loose, so judge well tonight: every soul you send fights for someone.
decree.d20: Ragnarök. Heimdall has blown the horn and the dead are coming all at once. Every rule stands. Judge as many as you can before the sun goes out.
shop.registryIndex.text: Skögul's tabs on the registry's edge. Searching it takes 2 seconds less.
shop.lensPolish.text: A cloth and a jar of fat for the rune-lens. Reading runes takes half the time.
shop.whetstone.text: Keeps the clippers keen. Clipping takes 2 seconds less.
shop.hornOfBrass.text: A louder question gets a quicker answer. Questioning costs 10 seconds instead of 20.
shop.waterClock.text: Measures the sun's last hour exactly, so none of it is wasted. Each shift gets 60 more seconds.
shop.goldFeather.text: A feather from her own cloak. It stirs at the faintest breath: the feather test takes 3 seconds.
shop.whaleLamp.text: Burns clean after dusk. Each shift gets 45 more seconds.
shop.runeTable.text: Every rune carved on one slate, by the lens. Reading runes takes 2 seconds.
shop.silverHorn.text: The dead answer before you've finished asking. Questioning costs 6 seconds.
ending.naglfar.title: Naglfar sails early
ending.naglfar.text: You left the nails long and took Loki's bargain. The ship of dead men's nails leaves the north two days before the gods are ready. Loki keeps his word to you, in his way: your family is aboard, and so are you. DRAFT.
ending.rebirth.title: The green earth
ending.rebirth.text: You learned what Odin knew and chose anyway. The host you sent holds long enough. After the fire, a new earth rises from the sea, green and unsown, and among the few who walk out onto it are the people you kept alive. DRAFT.
ending.smuggled.title: Smuggled home
ending.smuggled.text: The ferryman takes your rings and asks nothing. While the gods look the other way, your family crosses to a shore the wolf will never reach. You go back to the gate alone. Someone has to. DRAFT.
ending.transfer.title: The transfer
ending.transfer.text: The clerk's contract was generous and full of small print. When the horn blows, you are reassigned to a warmer room in another department, with a pension. DRAFT.
ending.hel.title: Hel's steward
ending.hel.text: Hel remembers who filled her hall when the gods wanted only heroes. After the fire, she makes you steward of the quiet dead, and you are good at it. DRAFT.
ending.freyja.title: Freyja's own
ending.freyja.text: You gave Freyja the souls she wanted, whatever Odin said. At Ragnarök her field holds, and she takes you in among the chosen, the way Valkyries once were. DRAFT.
ending.odin.title: Chooser eternal
ending.odin.text: Odin's hall was full and the host was strong. He falls to the wolf anyway, as foretold, but not before he names you chooser for whatever world comes next. DRAFT.
ending.wolf.title: The wolf wins
ending.wolf.text: Too few worthy dead, too many who ran, and Naglfar full to the rails. The gods fall quickly. From the gate you watch the fire come. DRAFT.
ending.lastStand.title: The last stand
ending.lastStand.text: Twenty days at the gate. The host you chose fights, and falls, as the gods do. What comes after is not yours to judge. DRAFT.
case.thorvald16.today: Is it today? I was sure it was today.
case.thorvald16.bear: Something big trod on me in the hills last night. I never saw what.
case.thorvald16.fine: I feel fine, mostly. Is that bad?
case.hrolf.roof: Your brother mended my nets, so I helped him patch your roof.
case.hrolf.drum: Over the little one's bed. Tight as a drum now.
case.hrolf.winter: I meant to see the winter out. I nearly did.
case.solveig.frown: You're one of Ragna's. I'd know that frown anywhere.
case.solveig.herring: The herring were running. We said one more net.
case.solveig.loom: Tell them at home I left the loom threaded.
case.hallbjorn.paid: Ulf's kin? The fine's paid, I hear. The boy only carved what I drew.
case.hallbjorn.debt: Ulf's kin? Tell the jarl the boy only carved what I drew.
case.hallbjorn.real: Half the swords in the valley are mine. The better half.
case.hallbjorn.cousin: The jarl's cousin fought beside me with one of mine. It bent. He noticed.
case.thorvald9.again: You again! You sent me home last time. Nobody at home believed me.
case.thorvald9.songs: I was sure this time. They'd already started the songs.
case.thorvald9.seat: Is my seat still free? I told everyone I had a seat.
case.bard.ulf: Ulf? Planks at the next trestle. Good hands, sad face. Talks about you.
case.bard.nails: The foreman says never trim a nail. The ship needs every one.
case.bard.ship: It's a very big ship. I'm not sure it floats.
case.bjarni.list: The jarl's men came with a list of my customers. Somebody wrote letters.
case.bjarni.tally: That's my own tally. Best work I ever did.
case.bjarni.cold: Is it far, where I'm going? I've been cold since this morning.
case.bjarni.best: Best tallies on the coast. Read mine, if you like good work.
case.bjarni.hero: Families wanted heroes. I only carved what they paid for.
case.bjarni.bench: Is there a carvers' bench, where you're sending me?
case.thrand.spear: I had them cut me with a spear, over the heart. The way Odin did.
case.thrand.poems: All my life I made poems about battles. I never saw one.
case.thrand.count: Does it count? Tell me it counts.
case.halla.born: I delivered you, you know. You had plenty to say even then.
case.halla.promise: Your mother made me promise to look for you at the gate. Here I am.
case.halla.loaf: There was a loaf for you. They took it off me at the bridge.
tm.oath.kept.4: I swore few oaths, and I kept every one.
tm.oath.kept.5: Oaths? I kept them all. It was easier than the alternative.
tm.oath.kept.6: Ask anyone at home. I kept my word, even when it cost me.
tm.owner.self.3: My {weapon}. My name's cut into it, if you read runes.
tm.owner.self.4: This {weapon} and I go back a long way.
tm.owner.self.5: I've carried this {weapon} since I could lift it.
tm.blade.ulfberht.3: My {weapon}'s an Ulfberht. Frankish steel. You don't see many.
tm.creed.heathen.3: The midwinter sacrifice every year, like my father. The old gods, all the way.
tm.creed.heathen.4: The old gods. Is that the right answer?
tm.creed.heathen.5: I've never been near a priest. Or a river with one in it.
tm.creed.baptized.3: A priest put me in the river and said I was the White Christ's now. I took his word for it.
tm.guise.3: I'm exactly what I look like. Nothing more.
tm.guise.4: No secrets here. I never had the head for them.
tm.guise.5: Me? I'm nobody special. Just me.
tm.guise.6: I'm what I look like. Tired, mostly.
tm.identity.7: {name} {patronym}. I've stood in more shield walls than you've stamped souls.
tm.identity.8: {name} {patronym}. Is this going to take long?
tm.identity.9: I think I'm {name}. {patronym}? That sounds right.
tm.identity.10: {name} {patronym}. Ask me anything you need to.
tm.death.battle.5: We met {foe} at {place}. They had more men. That's the whole story.
tm.death.battle.6: It was {place}. The fighting went on all morning, and I didn't see it end.
tm.death.battle.7: Killed at {place}, fighting {foe}. I'd do it again, just not today.
tm.death.battle.8: {place}. Go and ask {foe} how it went. The ones still standing.
tm.death.battle.9: {foe} at {place}. Same as every summer, apart from the last part.
tm.weapon.yes.3: They'll have to prise my {weapon} out of my fist.
tm.weapon.yes.4: I had my {weapon} to the end. Still have, look.
tm.weapon.yes.5: My {weapon} and I went down together. That's how it's done.
tm.weapon.yes.6: I never let go of my {weapon}. Couldn't, by the end.
tm.back.no.3: Nobody ever saw my back in a fight.
tm.back.no.4: Nobody can say I ran. Look me over, front and back.
tm.back.no.5: I did not run. I want that written down.
tm.back.no.6: I've never shown an enemy my back, and I wasn't going to start.
tm.flavor.braggart.2: You'll want a skald for this.
tm.flavor.braggart.3: Make sure they spell my name right in the hall.
tm.flavor.confused.2: Do I keep my boots on, or is it a boots-off hall?
tm.flavor.confused.3: Somebody should feed my goats. Can you tell somebody?
tm.flavor.coward.2: Do the halls have doors? Ones that bar from the inside?
tm.flavor.coward.3: Somewhere with no fighting would suit me. Or very little.
rv.muninn.forgot.2: Muninn: I knew this one. I did. The name's gone.
rv.muninn.forgot.3: Muninn: There was a name. It was on the tip of my beak.
rv.muninn.forgot.5: Muninn: I remember the face. Only the face.
rv.muninn.forgot.6: Muninn: Something with a horse in it? I'll think of it.
rv.muninn.identity.2: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Of course I know. I'm Memory.
rv.muninn.identity.3: Muninn: That's {name} {patronym}. I never forget. Hardly ever.
rv.muninn.heathen.2: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. The old gods, every feast, every year. I remember the smoke.
rv.muninn.oathKept.2: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Said a thing, did the thing. Every time.
rv.huginn.battle.2: Huginn: Fell at {place}. I was circling. I saw.
rv.huginn.battle.3: Huginn: {place}, in the thick of it. Didn't get up.
rv.huginn.sickness.2: Huginn: A fever took this one. Slowly.
rv.huginn.oldAge.2: Huginn: Outlived everyone. Went quietly, in the night.
rv.huginn.drowned.2: Huginn: Went over the side in a squall. Didn't come up.
rv.huginn.fledTrue.2: Huginn: Ran. Fast, too. Not fast enough.
rv.huginn.fledFalse.2: Huginn: No running. Not this one. I watched.
rv.huginn.fledFalse.3: Huginn: Didn't run. I'd have seen.
rv.huginn.weapon.2: Huginn: Held on to it to the end. I watched the whole thing.
rv.huginn.weapon.3: Huginn: Never let go of it. Not once.
rv.huginn.noWeapon.2: Huginn: Nothing in the hands at the end. Nothing at all.
tl.fled.false.2: Never showed the foe their back.
tl.outlaw.false.2: Broke no oath, sworn or spoken.
thread.owesSkogul: You owe Skögul the ten rings she advanced you.
thread.ulfDebt: Ulf still owes the jarl his share of the smith's fine.
thread.ulfShipyard: Ulf is shaping planks at a shipyard in the north, for a man with very clean hands.
thread.lokiDeal: The man with the scarred lips has your family's names, and room for them on his ship.
thread.ferry: The ferryman at the mouth of the fjord is holding places for your family. He wants a hundred rings more on the day the horn blows.
thread.woodKnown: Thorvald told you of Hoddmímir's wood, where nothing can find you.
thread.wood: Your family will wait out the end in Hoddmímir's wood.
thread.stayHome: Your family will stay home when the horn blows, together.
thread.clerkContract: You've signed the clerk's contract: a table in his department when the horn blows.
thread.truth: You've heard {n, plural, one {one thing} other {# things}} about what comes after the fire.
coach.d4.whim: New today: Freyja has claimed a share of the slain. Her whim for today is at the top of the rules: read it.
coach.d4.look: Now look for her whim on this soul.
coach.d4.stamp: Worthy, and just what Freyja asked for: she takes them. Stamp FÓLKVANGR, not VALHALLA.
coach.d5.lips: New today: the sea. Look at the lips.
coach.d5.stamp: Sea-foam on the lips: the sea took this one, and the drowned belong to Rán. Stamp RÁN.
coach.d6.registry: New today: the registry of outlaws and oathbreakers. Look this soul up in it.
coach.d6.stamp: Their name is in it. Outlaws and oathbreakers go to Hel, however well they died. Stamp HEL.
coach.d7.lens: New today: the rune-lens. A weapon carries its owner's name. Read this one's.
coach.d7.owner: The name on the blade isn't theirs: they borrowed it. Only a warrior's own weapon counts.
coach.d7.stamp: Whoever fell with someone else's weapon goes to Hel. Stamp HEL.
coach.d8.nails: New today: Naglfar is built from dead men's nails. Look at the hands.
coach.d8.clip: Nails left long go to the ship. Clip them before you send the soul on.
coach.d8.stamp: Clipped. The clippers don't change where a soul goes: judge this one as you would have.
coach.d10.neck: New today: the clerk of the White Christ. Look at what this soul wears at the neck.
coach.d10.stamp: A cross alone: baptized, so the clerk takes them. Stamp TRANSFER. A hammer beside the cross means only prime-signed, and they stay yours.
coach.d11.tally: This soul brought a saga tally. Read it.
coach.d11.lens: New today: forgers. Hold the rune-lens over the tally: a forger gets a rune wrong.
coach.d11.stamp: Forged. A forged tally counts for nothing: judge by the body alone.
coach.d12.lips: New today: Loki walks among the dead. Look closely at the lips.
coach.d12.stamp: Scars where the lips were sewn: the dwarf Brokkr sewed Loki's mouth shut. Whoever he says he is, stamp DETAIN.
coach.d13.ravens: New today: both ravens speak. Huginn saw how they died; Muninn remembers how they lived. Read them.
coach.d13.stamp: The ravens never lie, but they can seem to disagree. When they do, the Order of Judgment decides: the first rule that fits wins.
coach.d14.rules: New today: Hel's hall is full. Until she has room, those who died in their beds go to the clerk.
coach.d14.skin: How did this one die? Look at the skin.
coach.d14.stamp: Sickness or old age, and nothing earlier in the Order claims them: stamp TRANSFER, not HEL.
coach.d15.claims: New today: Odin names his own claim each day, as Freyja does. Both are at the top of the rules.
coach.d15.stamp: This soul fits both. When Odin and Freyja both want a worthy soul, Odin's claim wins. Stamp VALHALLA.
coach.d16.catch: New today: a worthy soul caught lying forfeits the hall. This one lies. Catch it: tap what they say, then what shows it false.
coach.d16.stamp: Caught. The halls of the worthy won't take a liar. Stamp HEL.
coach.d17.chest: New today: Odin's mark. Look over the heart.
coach.d17.stamp: A spear's cut, made before death: they were marked for Odin, and the marked go to Valhalla, even from their beds. Stamp VALHALLA.
twist.freyja: Freyja is greedy this round: her whim fits more of the worthy than usual.
twist.sea: A fleet went down in the night. The sea gives up its dead.
twist.forgers: The carvers have been busy. More souls than usual bring saga tallies, and not every tally is honest.
twist.loki: Loki has brought friends. Watch the lips.
twist.muninn: Muninn is tired. He forgets more than he remembers this round.
ach.odin.text: Keep Odin's hall full to the end, and be named chooser for the world after.
ach.freyja.text: Give Freyja the souls she asked for, and be taken in among her own.
ach.hel.text: Fill the quiet hall, and be made its steward.
ach.naglfar.text: Leave the nails long, take Loki's bargain, and sail early.
ach.transfer.text: Sign the clerk's contract and take the warmer room.
ach.smuggled.text: Pay the ferryman to take your family where the wolf can't follow.
ach.rebirth.text: Learn what Odin knew, and walk your family out onto the green earth.
ach.wolf.text: Watch the fire come from the gate.
ach.lastStand.text: Judge all twenty days, and see the host you chose fight and fall.
ach.stitched.title: Stitched
ach.unlucky.title: Unlucky, not dead
ach.unlucky.text: Send Thorvald the Unlucky home the first time he comes, and the last.
ach.nobodyLeft.title: Nobody left behind
ach.nobodyLeft.text: Reach Ragnarök with your whole family still at home.
ach.spotless.title: Spotless
ach.spotless.text: Judge every soul rightly on a campaign day, Day 10 or later.
